headline: Reported C-PACER adoption recommendation and proposed transportation and recreation impact fee increases.
summary: The meeting covered the 2050 Master Plan update, impact fees, and zoning amendments. Members approved the prior meeting minutes and nominated Alex Stoyle as primary and Ari Pollack as alternate representatives on the Planning Board's Master Plan Advisory Subcommittee. The Ad-Hoc Impact Fee Committee reached consensus on changes to impact fee waivers and to transportation and recreation fees.
decisions: Approved the August 25, 2026 meeting minutes unanimously.
Approved Alex Stoyle as primary and Ari Pollack as alternate representatives on the Master Plan Advisory Subcommittee, unanimously, with Pollack abstaining.
Ad-Hoc Impact Fee Committee reached consensus to change impact fee waivers and adjust transportation and recreation fees, and to research a fee for Police Station and middle school debt.
Fiscal Policy Advisory Committee voted to recommend that the City Council adopt the C-PACER program.
Planning Board approved amendments to the Site Plan Review Regulations for parking, circulation, and loading.

decision_evidence.quote: Bobby Segal moved to approve the minutes as presented. Emily Ricard seconded. The motion was approved unanimously.

After additional discussion, Chuck Gilboy moved to nominate Alex Stoyle to be EDAC’s primary representative on the Advisory Subcommittee, and Ari Pollack to serve as the alternate member. Bobby Segal seconded the motion. The motion carried unanimously.

It was noted that the Ad-Hoc Impact Fee Committee met on September 1, 2026 and it was the consensus of the Ad-Hoc Committee to proceed as follows: ... Research the potential cost to develop an impact fee to support debt service costs for the new Police Station and Concord School District Middle School.
Mayor Champlin reported that the City’s Fiscal Policy Advisory Committee (FPAC) met on September 21st and voted to recommend that the City Council adopt the C-PACER program.
(The Planning Board has already approved corresponding amendments to the Site Plan Review Regulations pertaining to parking, circulation, and loading).
